@: Kaldor's castle. Black stone, red windows, and spikes on every edge that could hold a spike.
It does not look like a place anyone has ever been invited to.
3: The gate, behind the moat. You'd need the bridge down to get anywhere near it.
~: The moat. Black, still, and deeper than it looks. Something under the surface is keeping very still too.
2: The drawbridge chains run up into the gatehouse. Somebody has to let it down.
o: A skull on a pike. A small sign underneath: HE CHALLENGED THE KING. HE LOST.
&: A dead tree. Nothing grows near the castle for long.
i: The guard post. A brazier burns on its roof day and night, so the castle can always see who's coming.
t: A soldier, flat on his back on the training sand. Out cold. A small bird has landed on his breastplate.
Nobody has the heart to move it.
z: Training sand, churned to mud and stamped flat again.
e: A straw dummy, beaten almost bald.
k: A rack of practice weapons. These ones are not wooden.
n: The fist crushing a crown, on a black pole.
x: A cook fire. Something on the spit was a rabbit once. Possibly twice.
X: An iron cage, door open. Empty, for now.
q: A barrel of salt pork. The army marches on its stomach. This army mostly stands about on it.
c: A lantern on a post, the one warm light on the grounds.
_: The castle road, back down through the forest to Warrior City.

objects.name: Captain Orsk
lines: Go on, then. Before I change my mind. I will not change my mind.

objects.name: Gate Guard
lines: We don't get paid. In case you were wondering.

questions.ask: What do you get instead of pay?
answer: Bread. Kaldorbread. Tessa bakes it in town. It's the only bread allowed and it tastes of being told off.
Some weeks Captain Orsk gives us a nod. Those are good weeks.

questions.ask: Unpaid and still this bad at it?
answer: Bad? I let you in, didn't I? That's the job done. Unpaid. Perfectly.
* He stares straight ahead, as if you were a draught.

questions.ask: What are you drilling them for?
answer: THE WAR! Which war? THE WAR! When? TOMORROW! It's always tomorrow! ONE! TWO!
Between you and me, the dummy's my best recruit. Never misses a day. Knocked out Harl.
Harl swung, the dummy swung back. It doesn't. That's the worrying part.
The medic's on it. The medic is always on it. ONE! TWO!
I CAN COUNT TO THREE. I CHOOSE NOT TO. THREE IS FOR OFFICERS.
* He goes back to ONE, TWO, a little louder, a little more personally.
Thrust. Parry. Thrust. Parry. Wonder about lunch. Thrust.
That third one isn't official. Everyone does it.
…Am I? Nobody's ever said. Four hundred years and nobody's ever said.
* He keeps drilling, slightly differently, and much worse.

objects.name: Soldier
lines: Sixteen hours a day. The king says strength is everything.

answer: The king. He says it at the window. Loudly. Sometimes to the window.
The queens say he's been off lately. Asks the chandelier about the war. The chandelier's very quiet on it.

questions.ask: Sixteen hours and arms like string?
answer: Wiry. The word is wiry.
* He flexes. Nothing visible happens. He seems satisfied anyway.

objects.name: Soldier
lines: My arms stopped hurting in the third century.

questions.ask: The third century? How old are you?
answer: Old enough. Nobody ages much in Kaldor's kingdom. Nobody gets out much either. Funny, that.
Gudrun in town's older than me. Does chin-ups on the cage bars. Makes me feel lazy.

questions.ask: Three centuries and still a private?
answer: Promotions need paperwork. Paperwork needs pay. Nobody gets paid.
So, yes. Three centuries. Still a private. Thank you for counting.

objects.name: Soldier
lines: We march on the wizards tomorrow.
We've been marching tomorrow for four hundred years.

answer: The king wakes up, says 'tomorrow', and goes back to talking to the walls.
The walls never argue. Good for morale, I suppose. Theirs.
We'd lose tomorrow too. That's why we keep it there.
* He marches on the spot, very defiantly, nowhere.

objects.name: Soldier
lines: Don't look at Harl. Harl's fine.

answer: He's breathing. The medic counts that as fine. The dummy counts it as a draw.
Harl's my mate. Owes me a Kaldorbread. If he doesn't wake up I'm not getting it.

questions.ask: Harl looks better than you, honestly.
answer: He's lying down. Everyone looks better lying down.
…I'll tell him you said that. When he's up. He'll be chuffed.

objects.name: Field Medic
lines: He took a dummy to the head. The dummy won.
Harl? Harl. How many fingers am I holding up? ...Wrong. It was a trick question. I'm not holding any up.

answer: Concussed, cold, and dreaming about soup. He keeps saying 'soup'. I've no soup.
Sister Hild in town has a bucket and a stool for the brawlers. She's better stocked than me. She's got yarn.

questions.ask: Are you even a real medic?
answer: I'm a chaplain. I was told 'close enough' by a man with a very big axe.
* He holds up three fingers at you. You are not sure it was a question.

objects.name: Soldier
lines: The shadows do the night watch now.
They don't eat, they don't sleep, they don't talk. Rubbish company.

answer: Came with the French adviser. Or the tall one. Nobody saw them arrive. Nobody saw anything. That's sort of the point of them.
Tallow keeps the braziers lit so they know where to stand. They stand there. All night.
Not replaced. Relieved. There's a difference.
…There isn't, is there. I'm going to sit nearer the fire.

objects.name: Soldier
lines: The king's new adviser, the French one, gave me this cheese.

answer: It's blue. Bread isn't blue. Swords aren't blue. Why is the cheese blue?
And he smiled when he gave it. I've lived here four hundred years. Nobody smiles when they give you anything.
You go and eat it, then. Go on. I'll watch.
* He holds the cheese out at arm's length. You both stare at it. It wins.

objects.name: Tallow
lines: Don't mind me. Braziers. Every one lit, every hour, or it's the cage for Tallow.
The king likes it bright out here. So he can see who's coming.

answer: Orders. Light all round, so the king can see who's coming a mile off.
And so the shadows know where to stand. Don't ask me what that means. I don't ask.
The king. The French fellow. And the tall one. Don't. He doesn't talk. Used to, they say. Nearly won, they say.
I light a brazier for him too. Nobody told me to. Nobody told me not to.
The shadows break quick on anybody strong. On anybody else, they don't break at all.
Come back strong. You didn't hear that from Tallow.

questions.ask: Named after candle grease, were you?
answer: Named after my dad. He was named after candle grease. It's a family trade.
…On you go, then. Tallow'll leave the one by the door unlit. Just for you.
